title: Lifting a prescribed next differential into the cycles
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal and $\mathcal P$ a class of $R$-modules. Assume its members are projective; whenever $M_1,M_{12}\in\mathcal P$ and $M_{12}\cong M_1\oplus M_2$, also $M_2\in\mathcal P$; and every map between members of $\mathcal P$ that is surjective after extension of scalars to $R/I$ is surjective. Put $F=(R/I)\otimes_R-$. Let $C$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], zero above an integer $b$, with terms in $\mathcal P$ and exact in degrees greater than an integer $n$. Let $E$ be an acyclic integer cochain complex of $R/I$-modules, and $q:FC\to E$ a morphism inducing term isomorphisms in all degrees at least $n$. Given $M\in\mathcal P$ and an isomorphism $e:FM\cong E^{n-1}$, there is a map $d:M\to C^n$ with $dd_C^n=0$, with $M\to C^n\to C^{n+1}$ exact, and with $F(d)q^n=e d_E^{n-1}$.

proof.text: Obtain the cycle object Z, its membership in P, and its kernel sequence both before and after scalar extension from lem-sc-acyclic-lift-split-cycles.

Compose e, the incoming differential of E and the inverse of q^n to form a:F(M)->F(C^n). The comparison square and the square-zero equation of E show that a is killed by F(d_C^n). The mapped kernel universal property supplies g:F(M)->F(Z). Acyclicity of E and injectivity of the two comparison/kernel inclusions show elementwise that g is surjective.

Apply Mathlib TensorProduct.mk_surjective and Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective to prove that the quotient adjunction unit Z->restrict(F(Z)) is surjective. Projectivity of M factors the adjoint transpose of g through this unit. Adjunction naturality gives F(t)=g for the resulting t:M->Z. The surjectivity hypothesis gives surjectivity of t. Compose with the cycle inclusion; the original kernel sequence and surjectivity of t give exactness, and the defining equation of g gives the required comparison square.

theorem exists_acyclicLift_nextDifferential
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (P : ModuleCat.{max u v} R → Prop)
    (hprojective : ∀ M, P M → Projective M)
    (hsummand : ∀ M₁ M₂ M₁₂ : ModuleCat.{max u v} R,
      P M₁ → P M₁₂ → Nonempty (M₁₂ ≅ ModuleCat.of R (M₁ × M₂)) → P M₂)
    (hsurjective : ∀ (M₁ M₂ : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (f : M₁ ⟶ M₂),
      P M₁ → P M₂ →
      Function.Surjective ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).map f) →
      Function.Surjective f)
    (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ)
    (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R ⧸ I)) ℤ)
    (q : ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj C ⟶ E)
    (b n : ℤ) (hupper : C.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hP : ∀ i, P (C.X i)) (hexact : ∀ i, n < i → C.ExactAt i)
    (hq : ∀ i, n ≤ i → IsIso (q.f i)) (hE : E.Acyclic)
    (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (hM : P M)
    (e : (ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj M ≅ E.X (n - 1)) :
    ∃ d : M ⟶ C.X n, ∃ hd : d ≫ C.d n (n + 1) = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk d (C.d n (n + 1)) hd).Exact ∧
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).map d ≫ q.f n =
        e.hom ≫ E.d (n - 1) n
